text: . Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal has described Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s two-day State Visit to India as a historic milestone, saying it has brought Nepal-India relations back on a positive track and opened new avenues for bilateral cooperation.Briefing the media at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu after Prime Minister Shah’s return from India, Khanal said the visit focused on strengthening the longstanding partnership between the two neighbouring countries and ensuring tangible benefits for their people.The Foreign Minister also highlighted India’s development assistance package worth 240 billion Nepali rupees, including 56 billion rupees in grants for post-disaster reconstruction and infrastructure projects, and 184 billion rupees in lines of credit for energy-sector projects.Mr Khanal said the two countries had also agreed to make the existing Kathmandu-Bhairahawa-Lucknow air route bidirectional. Eight agreements were signed in areas including security, education, health, traditional medicine, satellite communication and sustainable urban development.He further highlighted the inauguration of the Janakpur-Ayodhya passenger train service, the launch of the second phase of the Motihari-Amlekhgunj petroleum pipeline and the laying of the foundation stone for the Lower Arun Hydropower Project.The two Prime Ministers also unveiled a Joint Vision Document titled ‘Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal’, outlining cooperation in connectivity, energy, trade, agriculture, education, health, digital services, innovation and climate resilience. The two countries also agreed to review existing bilateral agreements, including the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, on the basis of mutual consent.Khanal expressed confidence that the visit would provide a strong foundation for result-oriented cooperation and further strengthen diplomatic, economic and development ties between the two countries.

. The United States and Qatar have agreed to deepen cooperation in defence, security, trade, investment and emerging technologies during the eighth US-Qatar Strategic Dialogue held in Washington, DC.The dialogue was co-chaired by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Qatar’s Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani. The talks focused on expanding bilateral ties, regional security and economic cooperation as the two countries prepare to mark the 55th anniversary of their diplomatic relations.In a joint statement, both sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the strategic partnership and expanding economic and investment opportunities. The discussions also covered cooperation in artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity and critical mineral supply chains.The two countries signed a Critical Minerals Framework to diversify supply chains and enhance global economic resilience. On the defence front, the two sides reviewed progress under the 38-billion-dollar US-Qatar defence cooperation agreement and discussed enhancing Qatar’s integrated air and missile defence capabilities.Both countries reiterated their commitment to ensuring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, underlining its importance for regional security, energy supplies and global economic stability.

. In Men’s Cricket, New Zealand scored 119 for 2 at stumps on Day Four of the first Test against India in their second innings at Wellington.Earlier, the Visitors declared their first innings at a record 720 for 9, taking a huge lead of 352 runs over New Zealand’s first-innings score of 368. India’s total of 720 is their highest-ever Test score outside India and the 18th-highest total in Test cricket history.India also created two major records and became the first team to have their top five batters score 80 or more runs in the same innings. They also became the first team to build partnerships of 50 or more runs for each of the first seven wickets.For Visitors, KL Rahul played a key role at the top of the order. He became the first Indian opener to score a Test century in all four SENA countries South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.

. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in New Delhi is showcasing its flagship health programmes and public healthcare initiatives. The theme of this year’s Health Pavilion is Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat, highlights preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a healthier nation. The Pavilion was inaugurated by NITI Aayog Member, Dr M Srinivas, in the presence of Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Srinivas emphasised on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyle choices to address rising burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions. He also highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs. Outlining the benefits of Health Pavilion, Dr. Srinivas said that it offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He also encouraged visitors to actively participate in the Pavilion’s activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.The Ministry noted that in the Pavilion 39 stalls representing 24 national health programmes and organisations showcase Government’s healthcare initiatives, achievements and services. The Ministry also highlighted that a dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology. The Pavilion also included interactive activities, live cpr demonstrations, health awareness sessions and dedicated kids’ zone to engage visitors and promote healthy living. The Ministry said that the Pavilion provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government’s wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. On the 2nd day of the ongoing 43rd Indian Oil Servo Surjit Hockey Tournament in Jalandhar, the Punjab Police team secured an impressive victory by defeating CAG Delhi 3-1 in a Pool-C match, today. In Pool-D, the Punjab & Sind Bank (Delhi) team defeated CRPF (Delhi) 1-0. Whereas defending champions Indian Oil advanced to the quarter-finals by defeating Rail Coach Factory, Kapurthala 2-0.Tomorrow, Nov 24th, CAG Delhi will take on Indian Navy Mumbai at 2:15 PM. Indian Air Force will play with CRPF, Delhi at 3:45 PM and the match between PNB Delhi and Army XI Delhi is scheduled at 5:30 PM.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed happiness over Shiromani Akali Dal joining the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) today. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that this is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress. The Prime Minister added that nurtured by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, L K Advani and Parkash Singh Badal, the Akali Dal-BJP Alliance has stood the test of time. He also expressed confidence that the alliance will emerge as the preferred choice of the people of Punjab.

. India has called for an immediate end to attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Black Sea, urging the restoration of safe navigation through international waterways amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict.Addressing a high-level briefing at the United Nations Security Council, India’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish, said the conflict had far-reaching global consequences, particularly for food security, energy supplies and international trade. He reiterated India’s readiness to contribute to all efforts towards a peaceful resolution, emphasising that dialogue and diplomacy remained the way forward.Highlighting the importance of the Black Sea region to global food security, the Indian envoy said Russia and Ukraine together account for nearly a quarter of global exports of wheat, maize and barley. He noted that disruptions to shipping and agricultural trade disproportionately affect countries of the Global South.Mr Harish also expressed concern over attacks on merchant vessels in the Black Sea, which had resulted in the deaths and disappearance of several Indian seafarers. He referred to attacks involving the vessels MV Omorfi, MV Royad Mammadov, MV Golden Leo and MV AGN RAGNAR.He said India was engaging with both Russia and Ukraine on the safety of commercial shipping and seafarers, as well as the restoration of grain export corridors. Mr Harish further highlighted the launch of the Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers by India and Liberia at the United Nations, aimed at strengthening international cooperation on maritime safety.Reiterating India’s position, he said safe commercial shipping and uninterrupted flows of food, fertilisers and energy were essential for global stability, particularly for vulnerable countries.

. A road accident involving a collision between a passenger bus and a truck on Al Watan Road in the Emirate of Ras Al Khaimah has claimed 11 lives, the UAE’s Ministry of Interior has said.The Ministry said that the relevant emergency teams were dispatched to the accident site immediately after receiving the report. They began rescue and emergency response operations in coordination with ambulance services, Civil Defence and other concerned authorities.Investigations into the circumstances and causes of the accident are ongoing. The Ministry stated that the findings would be announced once the investigations have been completed.This is the second major traffic accident in the UAE this month. On 12 November, a pile-up involving 18 cars and five lorries on Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Road in Fujairah left 14 people dead, including four Indian nationals.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.

. Labour unrest continued in Bangladesh’s Gazipur industrial belt on Tuesday, as garment workers demanding higher minimum wages blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway at several points, disrupting traffic and prompting police to use tear gas and sound grenades to disperse protesters, according to local media reports.Workers attempted to occupy the highway between Bhabanipur and Maona Chourasta in Sreepur, bringing traffic to a standstill in both directions. Police and workers were involved in several rounds of clashes and chases.Factory authorities in several areas, including Member Bari, Bhabanipur and Bagher Bazar, announced closures amid growing security concerns.Separately, protests erupted in Gazipur’s Konabari area following rumours about the death of a garment worker. Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse workers who had blocked a regional road.Meanwhile, workers at 10 factories in the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt abstained from work, demanding a wage increase. Around 20 factories in the area reportedly remain closed indefinitely under the Labour Act.Additional law enforcement personnel have been deployed in industrial areas amid fears of further escalation. No immediate reports of casualties were available.

. In the bullion market, gold and silver prices witnessed a steep decline over the past week as a stronger US dollar and elevated Treasury yields weighed heavily on investor sentiment. For the second week in a row, precious metals remained under pressure as expectations grew that the US Federal Reserve would maintain its hawkish stance to bring inflation back within its 2 per cent target range.At the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), Gold futures for December contract plunged 10.9 per cent to settle at 1 lakh 21 thousand 778 rupees per 10 grams during the week. Silver futures for December contract tumbled almost 16.2 per cent to close at 1 lakh 47 thousand 813 rupees per kilogram.Meanwhile, at the Commodity Exchange (COMEX), Gold futures for the December contract plummeted 9.5 per cent during the week to settle at 3515.4 dollars per troy ounce. Silver futures for the December contract nosedived 16.4 per cent over the week to end at 41.07 dollars per troy ounce.

. World Fisheries Day is being observed today. The day aims to highlight the importance of sustainable fisheries and aquaculture in ensuring food and nutritional security, generating livelihoods and maintaining ecological balance. The observance traces its origins to 1997, when representatives from 18 countries gathered in New Delhi to establish the World Fisheries Forum. The initiative aimed to promote responsible fishing practices and safeguard the rights and interests of fishing communities.The theme for World Fisheries Day 2026 is “Empowering People for Change: Advancing Decent Work in Fisheries and Aquaculture, Particularly for Youth and Women.” The theme highlights the need to promote decent employment opportunities, empower women and young people, and ensure inclusive and sustainable growth across the fisheries and aquaculture sectors.India is the world’s second-largest fish-producing country, accounting for nearly eight per cent of global fish production. The country has made significant progress in the sector over the past decade. India’s total fish production has more than doubled, rising from 96 lakh tonnes to 195 lakh tonnes last year. The fisheries sector is an important pillar of the Indian economy, supporting the livelihoods of millions of people. A coordinated approach involving all stakeholders is aimed at further strengthening the sector, with a focus on increasing fish production, boosting exports and creating more livelihood opportunities.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the Sikh tradition has always symbolised the spirit of sacrificing everything for the nation and its culture. He was speaking after attending Shabad Kirtan at Lok Niwas, the residence of Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, in New Delhi.Quoting the teachings of Guru Nanak Dev, the Prime Minister said that his principles had been an integral part of his life. Mr Modi said that during the most difficult periods of India’s history, the Sikh Gurus had kept alive the spirit of national protection and cultural identity.On the occasion of Guru Nanak Dev’s Parkash Purab, the Prime Minister also extended greetings to citizens. In a social media post, he said that Guru Nanak Dev’s timeless teachings continue to guide humanity. Mr Modi expressed hope that his message would inspire citizens to build a society rooted in kindness, togetherness and the welfare of all.

. The documentary film Sky Beyond Borders – Tarang Shakti showcases India’s cultural strength and its spirit of unity and collaboration beyond its military capabilities.Speaking to the media during the red-carpet event on the fifth day of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 in Goa, the film’s director, Kanika Gautam, said it seeks to present to the world the diverse cultural values and traditions that define India. She said the film captures India’s cultural contributions through yoga, marathons and cultural programmes, reflecting the country’s unity and diversity.Director General, West Zone, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Smita Vats Sharma, said film festivals such as IFFI provide a powerful platform to showcase films from across the world and different parts of India. She highlighted that the festival brings together emerging and established directors, technical professionals and creative talent, celebrating India’s diversity and the power of cinema to connect people and cultures.Sky Beyond Borders – Tarang Shakti is a 14-minute English-language aviation documentary directed by Kanika Gautam. It is featured in the Gala Premieres section of the 57th IFFI 2026 in Goa.

. At the National Squash Championships 2026, Abhay Singh and Akanksha Salunkhe clinched singles titles. They were crowned the men’s and women’s champions at the National Squash Championships 2026, which concluded at the Otters Club in Mumbai yesterday. This was the 82nd edition of the senior squash nationals.Top seed Abhay Singh, who won a silver medal at the Asian Games 2026, got the better of second seed Veer Chotrani 3-0  in the men’s final. It was a third senior national title for world No. 26 Abhay, who was contesting his fifth consecutive final. Akanksha Salunkhe, meanwhile, came through qualifying to lift her first senior national crown on her third attempt, having lost her two previous finals.

. Armenia published a draft proposal for a new constitution on Monday, marking a significant step towards signing a formal peace agreement with long-time adversary Azerbaijan.The unveiling of the document puts pressure on Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan to secure a deal with Baku after he won a new term in office in June in an election widely viewed as a referendum on his handling of the peace process.Armenia and Azerbaijan, neighbouring countries in the South Caucasus, have been at war intermittently since the late 1980s, mainly over the mountainous region of Nagorno-Karabakh. The region was controlled for decades by ethnic Armenians but was recaptured by Azerbaijan in a lightning offensive in 2023. The two countries signed a joint, US-backed peace declaration last August.For Azerbaijan, however, a key sticking point in signing a formal agreement has been the preamble to Armenia’s Constitution, which refers to another Soviet-era document calling for the reunification of Armenia and Nagorno-Karabakh, then an autonomous region within Soviet Azerbaijan.The proposed new Constitution rewrites the preamble and removes the reference to which Baku has objected.

. Stories rooted in human emotions can connect with audiences across languages and generations, said filmmaker Mahesh Limaye at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). He was speaking about his Marathi film, Aadi Anant.Mr Limaye said the film’s story reminded him of caring for his father during his final days. Written by actor Sankarshan Karhade, the film follows an aspiring actor and his grandfather as their affectionate relationship is tested by an accident and the responsibilities of caregiving. The director said its themes of family bonds, ambition and responsibility could resonate with audiences beyond the Marathi-speaking community.Mr Limaye said mutual respect between Ashok Saraf and Karhade helped bring the relationship between the two generations to the screen. He recalled that Saraf approached the role with the enthusiasm of a newcomer.He added that while exposure to technology may have changed the outlook of the younger generation, their emotional needs remain similar to those of earlier generations. Mr Limaye also welcomed the emergence of new Marathi filmmakers, saying fresh voices and innovative subjects were important for the industry’s future.Aadi Anant is featured in the Indian Panorama section of IFFI.

. Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia has said that India has moved from being a consumer of technology to becoming a creator of technology. He was addressing the Telecom Startups and MSME Conclave 2026 in New Delhi.Mr Scindia said India’s startup ecosystem had grown from just a few hundred startups in 2014 to more than two lakh today. He added that the country now has over 110 crore internet connections, compared to 25 crore in 2014.Mr Scindia said India had also progressed from around six crore broadband connections to over 104 crore, while the total number of telephone connections had crossed 133 crore. He underlined that data costs had fallen by 97 per cent, from ₹269 per GB in March 2014 to ₹8 per GB. The Minister said the country was moving towards self-reliance and that the world would soon rely on India. Highlighting the importance of MSMEs, he described them as the backbone of the economy.During the event, Mr Scindia inaugurated an exhibition featuring startups and MSMEs. It brought together telecom startups, MSMEs, industry leaders and other stakeholders to showcase indigenous telecom technologies, discuss challenges faced by domestic innovators and explore opportunities to scale up and commercialise homegrown telecom solutions. The event also provided startups and MSMEs with an opportunity to showcase their innovative products and solutions through dedicated exhibition stalls.

. The combined Index of Core Industries (ICI) registered growth of 10.9 per cent in October on an annual basis driven by strong performance in iron ore, coal, electricity and cement sectors. This is higher than the upwardly revised growth rate of 8.2 per cent recorded in September. According to the provisional estimates released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry today, six out of nine core sectors recorded positive growth last month. Among these, iron ore production recorded the highest growth at 26.4 per cent. Coal production accelerated by 23.1 per cent, electricity generation increased by 21.6 per cent, cement production gained 15.4 per cent, steel production output grew by 7.3 per cent, and refinery products expanded by 3.4 per cent on an annual basis. However, natural gas production fell by 7.6 per cent, crude oil production dipped by 4.1 per cent, and fertilizer production declined by 12.2 per cent in October on an annual basis.

. An earthquake measuring 5.6 on the local magnitude scale struck near Olangchung Gola in Taplejung district, close to the Nepal-Tibet border, this morning.According to Nepal’s National Earthquake Monitoring and Research Centre (NEMRC), the earthquake occurred at 7:17 AM local time.Tremors were also felt in Kathmandu.Further details about the impact of the earthquake are awaited.

. India has invoked the 1943 Bengal famine at the UN Security Council to highlight the disproportionate impact of conflicts on the Global South, calling for measures to prevent food insecurity amid the Ukraine war.Speaking at a high-level briefing of the UN Security Council yesterday, India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, said that developing countries were bearing the brunt of food, fuel, fertiliser and energy shortages caused by global conflicts.He called for the protection of Black Sea food supply routes, civilian infrastructure, freedom of navigation and humanitarian access to prevent worsening food, fuel and fertiliser crises.Recalling Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s message that the world has to move from endless war to the end of war, he reiterated India’s readiness to contribute to all efforts towards a peaceful resolution of the conflict. He also stressed that Prime Minister Modi had firmly stood with the Global South when he said that “this is not an era of war”.At the Council, India urged an end to attacks on commercial vessels and seafarers, citing incidents in which Indian crew members were killed or went missing. It also highlighted its food assistance to countries including Afghanistan, Sudan and Palestine.

. Under the theme ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ (Development and Heritage), women-led Self-Help Groups (SHGs) from Tripura, along with various wings under the Department of Industries and Commerce, are participating in the international trade fair being held in New Delhi.At the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, the Tripura Pavilion is showcasing a wide range of products manufactured by the state’s Self-Help Groups, along with an impressive collection of bamboo and cane handicrafts.Tripura Industries and Commerce Minister Santana Chakma visited the state’s stalls and encouraged the women entrepreneurs, appreciating their efforts. She said their contribution is significant in strengthening Tripura’s economy. She further stated that participation in such fairs would help promote products manufactured in Tripura and increase their recognition in the global market.It may be mentioned that Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal inaugurated the fair on November 13. The exhibition will continue until November 27, with participation from representatives of more than 30 states and Union Territories across the country.

. In Table Tennis, India’s Boys Under-19 team has confirmed its first medal at the ITTF World Youth Championships in Istanbul, Türkiye, after storming into the semifinals. The Indian trio of Priyanuj Bhattacharya, Abhinandh Pradhivadhi and Balamurugan Rajasekaran produced a dominant performance, defeating hosts Türkiye 3-nil in the quarterfinals to seal a place in the last four and guarantee a medal for India. India will now face Chinese Taipei in the semifinals.Meanwhile, Indian Girls’ Under-19 team bowed out in the quarterfinals after suffering a nil-3 defeat to France. Divyanshi, Syndrela and Hansini lost their respective matches.

. Political tensions and security concerns continued in Bangladesh, with five leaders and activists of the Bangladesh Jatiotabadi Chhatra Dal shot in Pabna district, while the house of an accused Jubo League leader was set on fire following the attack, according to local media reports.The shooting took place on Monday evening in the Majhdia area of Sara Union in Ishwardi upazila, when unidentified assailants opened fire on the Chhatra Dal activists. The injured were initially taken to Ishwardi Upazila Health Complex and later referred to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment. The house of Imtiaz Hossain Milon Chowdhury, a former Chhatra League organisational secretary and Jubo League leader, was subsequently torched. Allegations of involvement in the shooting have been levelled against him and other Awami League activists.In a separate development, Detective Branch police detained Sheikh Ataur Rahman, general secretary of the Chattogram North district Awami League, from his residence in Oxygen, Chattogram. He is reportedly accused in three cases involving sabotage and disruption of law and order.Meanwhile, Border Guard Bangladesh has deployed 101 platoons across Dhaka and seven districts to maintain security. Surveillance has been strengthened around key installations, industrial areas and other sensitive locations.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading 0.6 per cent down at 91 US dollars and 44 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.2 per cent down at 82 US dollars and 27 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. India and Nepal have announced a series of initiatives covering connectivity, energy, trade, education, healthcare and institutional cooperation during Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s State Visit to India. The outcomes include a development assistance package worth 15,000 crore rupees, new cross-border infrastructure projects, expanded access to Indian ports for Nepal’s transit cargo and eight Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) across key sectors.Among the major announcements is the launch of the Sarayu-Kamala Express rail service connecting Ayodhya in India with Janakpur in Nepal.India and Nepal have adopted a Joint Vision Document, laying out a roadmap for a future-oriented partnership between the two countries. New Delhi also announced a development assistance package worth 24,000 crore Nepali rupees for the Himalayan nation.The two countries signed eight agreements to strengthen cooperation in various fields, including healthcare, traditional medicine, the establishment of a satellite communication network and capacity-building training programmes, among others.The agreements were signed following talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, in New Delhi yesterday. Both leaders held wide-ranging discussions on bilateral, regional and global issues.Later, in a joint press statement, Prime Minister Modi said India-Nepal relations are woven together by shared history, faith, culture and deep people-to-people ties. He also announced the Joint Vision Document adopted by the two nations.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold plunged nearly 4.4 per cent to 1,23,893 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver also tumbled over 4.9 per cent to 1,52,528 rupees per kilogram according to the closing rates of India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. S&P Global has projected India to be the fastest-growing economy in the Asia-Pacific region in 2027. The agency expects India’s economy to grow by 7 per cent in both the current fiscal year and the next fiscal year, ending March 2028. In its Economic Outlook Asia-Pacific Q1 2027 report, agency said India’s growth in the June and September quarters was driven by robust goods exports, government-led investment spending and strong household consumption, supported by buoyant credit growth.The Global firm also highlighted India’s growing integration into global supply chains, noting that export performance had benefited from trade diversification and the country’s expanding role in global manufacturing. Electronics, engineering goods and chemicals were among the sectors that recorded particular strength.S&P Global projects inflation to average 5.3 per cent in the current fiscal year ending March 2027, with risks tilted to the upside. However, it expects inflation to ease to 4.7 per cent in the fiscal year ending March 2028. Against this backdrop, the agency expects the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to raise policy rates by a further 25 basis points in December. It also said the likelihood of another rate hike in early 2027 had increased.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. The World Health Organization (WHO) has congratulated India on administering over 10 million doses of the HPV vaccine to 14-year-old girls. In a social media post, WHO described this as a significant milestone in the country’s efforts to prevent cervical cancer.It said the achievement reflects the collective commitment of the government, health workers, communities, parents and partners to protect girls from cervical cancer and ensure that every girl has access to the protection offered by HPV vaccination.Earlier, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also commended all stakeholders for their efforts in ensuring the administration of one crore HPV vaccine doses, covering nearly 87 per cent of the annual cohort of eligible girls.Sharing a social media post by Union Health Minister J. P. Nadda, PM Modi said this was a significant milestone in the journey towards preventive healthcare. He said every dose was a step towards protecting girls from cervical cancer and ensuring a healthier future for them.

. BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) will contest the upcoming 2027 Punjab Assembly polls together. Announcing the alliance at BJP party headquarters in New Delhi today, senior BJP leader and Home Minister Amit Shah said the senior leaders of both the parties sat together and took the decision that the next Punjab Assembly elections will be contested jointly. He expressed confidence that the NDA will come to power in Punjab assembly polls, saying that this alliance will be a symbol of Hindu-Sikh brotherhood. Mr Shah stated that getting rid of the drug and corruption menace in Punjab will be the topmost priority.The Home Minister said it is a matter of joy that the NDA’s oldest ally, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), is returning to the NDA once again today. He said that he spoke with Prime Minister Narendra Modi about the expansion of the NDA, and the Prime Minister also called the party presidents of both the BJP and the SAD and expressed the sentiment that the NDA is now complete.BJP President Nitin Nabin has described the alliance between the BJP and the Akali Dal as a natural alliance, saying it will strengthen the NDA and work towards the development of Punjab.Shriomoni Akali Dal President Sukhbir Singh Badal said that whenever the two parties formed governments together, Punjab witnessed progress, peace, stability and communal harmony.Ahead of announcing the alliance, BJP National President Nitin Nabin felicitated SAD President Sukhbir Singh Badal at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi.

. The 557th Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism, is being celebrated today with religious fervour and enthusiasm across the country and abroad. Guru Nanak Dev Ji was born on this day in 1469 to Mehta Kalu Ji and Mata Tripta Ji at Rai Bhoi Ki Talwandi, now known as Nankana Sahib in Pakistan, on the full moon day of the month of Katak. President Droupadi Murmu and Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan have extended greetings to Indians in the country and abroad on the occasion.Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji gave the message of ‘Ek Onkar’ (One God), opposed social evils such as casteism and emphasised the equality of all human beings.On this auspicious occasion, a large number of devotees have been paying obeisance at Gurdwaras across the country since morning.Gurdwara Ber Sahib at Sultanpur Lodhi in Punjab, where Guru Sahib meditated for 14 years, 9 months and 13 days, is reverberating with hymns as Kirtan Darbars and Gurbani Vichar are being held there and at other Gurdwaras, including Sri Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar. The joy of connecting with God is evident on the faces of devotees. Community kitchens are also being organised at various places.A delegation of Sikh pilgrims has also reached Gurdwara Sri Nankana Sahib, the birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev Ji in Pakistan, to pay obeisance. Deepmala and fireworks will be held at Sri Harmandir Sahib and other Gurdwaras this evening.In a social media post, President Droupadi Murmu said Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s message of ‘Ik Onkar’ signifies the unity of all humanity. She highlighted his teachings of equality, compassion, honest living and service, and urged people to follow his ideals for the welfare of society and the nation.Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan said Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s timeless teachings of truth, equality, compassion, selfless service and universal brotherhood continue to inspire people to build a society rooted in peace, harmony and mutual respect. He expressed hope that the message of Naam Japo, Kirat Karo and Vand Chhako would guide everyone towards righteousness and service to humanity.

. In Men’s Hockey, the Indian team clinched the three-match 2026 India-New Zealand Century of Sporting Unity Series 1-0 as the third and final match of the tour ended in a 2-2 draw at Lloyd Elsmore Hockey Stadium in Auckland.In the series decider played yesterday, New Zealand took an early lead with Dylan Thomas scoring the first goal in the ninth minute, but India responded with two goals in quick succession. Sanjay converted a penalty corner in the 16th minute to restore parity before Karthi Selvam scored a field goal two minutes later to give the visitors a 2-1 advantage. However, the hosts fought back in the final quarter, with Benji Culhane finding the equaliser in the 55th minute. Neither side managed to find a winner thereafter as the contest ended in a draw, confirming India’s series victory.India had edged New Zealand 3-2 in the opening match while the second match also ended in a 2-2 stalemate.The series also marked 100 years of sporting ties between India and New Zealand, dating back to 1926, when an Indian Army hockey team featuring the legendary Major Dhyan Chand became the first Indian team to tour New Zealand.

. In Men’s Cricket, the first Test between New Zealand and India ended in a draw. In reply to India’s 720 for 9 in first innings, New Zealand made 239 for 5 in their second innings. Akashvani correspondent reports that resuming the final day at 119 for two, Kiwis lost two well-set overnight batters in Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra. However, Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips stood firm for 43 overs as New Zealand batted out 120 overs in their second innings to salvage a draw in the first Test today.India had taken a 352-run first-innings lead after posting their highest-ever Test total in New Zealand, but could manage only three of the eight wickets they needed on the final day. The Visitors declared their first innings at a record 720 for 9, taking a huge lead of 352 runs over New Zealand’s first-innings score of 368. India also created two major records and became the first team to have their top five batters score 80 or more runs in the same innings.They also became the first team to build partnerships of 50 or more runs for each of the first seven wickets. For Visitors, KL Rahul played a key role at the top of the order. He became the first Indian opener to score a Test century in all four SENA countries South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.

. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Jitan Ram Manjhi today inaugurated the MSME Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 in New Delhi. On the occasion, Mr Manjhi interacted with artisans and exhibitors at various stalls. He highlighted the importance of khadi as a symbol of country’s rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship. The Minister said that khadi represents country’s traditional industry, entrepreneurship and art. Mr Manjhi also highlighted the PM Vishwakarma Yojana, which covers 18 traditional trades, including barbers, leather artisans, cobblers, garland makers and net weavers.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.

. Indian Railways operated around 18,000 additional trains during the festive season from October to November this year, accommodating lakhs of passengers daily.According to Indian Railways, around 20 crore passengers travelled by train during the 26-day peak festive period, registering an increase of 8 per cent over the corresponding period last year.It noted that during Durga Puja, the average daily passenger count increased from 70 lakh to 76 lakh. During Diwali, it rose from 71 lakh to 74 lakh, while during Chhath, the figure increased from 75 lakh to 82 lakh.

. In Mumbai, more than 22,500 runners, including 59 participants from 20 foreign countries, took part in the ninth edition of the Indian Oil Western Naval Command (WNC) Navy Half Marathon 2026. The event was flagged off from Cross Maidan by Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Western Naval Command. Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan also participated in the 21-km race.The marathon featured three categories: 21 km, 10 km and 5 km. The event aims to promote fitness, patriotism and camaraderie between the Indian Navy and civilians.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov held a telephone conversation to discuss bilateral cooperation and key international developments. The Russian Foreign Ministry said the two leaders discussed various issues on the bilateral agenda and exchanged views on current international matters.The conversation comes amid India’s continued diplomatic engagement with Russia and Ukraine to support efforts towards a peaceful resolution of the conflict. Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict should be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy.India has also been engaging with Russia, Ukraine, Europe and the United States on issues including the protection of civilian shipping and seafarers, the restoration of grain exports through the Black Sea and ensuring that energy infrastructure is not targeted.

. Market participants will focus on geopolitical developments, the final leg of the corporate earnings season, foreign portfolio investor (FPI) flows, commodity price movements and currency fluctuations for cues next week.Indian equity markets will remain closed on Tuesday on account of Gurpurab, the birth anniversary of Sri Guru Nanak Dev. Meanwhile, on the primary market front, two mainboard IPOs are scheduled to open for subscription, while two companies are set to make their stock market debut.In the United States, investors will closely monitor the upcoming Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data, along with the second estimate of third-quarter GDP growth. Meanwhile, market participants will also keep a close watch on the Bank of Korea’s upcoming monetary policy decision for cues on the global interest rate outlook.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has cautioned investors against relying on unofficial Grey Market Premium (GMP) figures to assess the likely listing prices or expected returns from upcoming Initial Public Offerings (IPOs). In an advisory issued today, SEBI said such pre-listing premium figures are unofficial, unverified and unregulated, as the transactions take place outside the regulated stock market framework, without investor protection or settlement guarantees.SEBI has advised all registered intermediaries and market participants to refrain from publishing or circulating GMP figures. It has also urged investors to avoid GMP-linked transactions and invest in IPOs only through SEBI-registered intermediaries and authorised platforms. The regulator has clarified that investors involved in such transactions will not have access to its or stock exchanges’ grievance redressal mechanisms.

. In Hockey, India thrashed Thailand 7-0 in their league-stage encounter of the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal this evening. Deepika led the charge with a brilliant hat-trick, while Navneet Kaur scored a brace.Mumtaz Khan and skipper Sunelita Toppo also scored one goal each. This was India’s third consecutive victory in the tournament, following their earlier wins over Malaysia and South Korea. With this win, India moved to the top of the points table with nine points.Earlier in the day, Malaysia registered a 3-1 victory over South Korea in their league-stage match, while Japan also secured a convincing 3-1 win against China.

. Anupama Ramachandran clinched her second consecutive world title at the IBSF World Women’s Snooker Championship in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, yesterday. She defeated Hong Kong’s So Man Yan 3-1 in the final to successfully retain her crown, which she won last year to become India’s first-ever female IBSF Snooker world champion. After conceding a 16-58 defeat in the first frame, Anupama bounced back to win the next three frames dominantly to conquer the title in front of a home crowd.

. Houthis have claimed that Saudi airstrikes on Monday have resulted in 25 persons being dead or missing in Yemen’s southwest.The Houthi military spokesperson had reported yesterday that Saudi forces carried out attacks targeting the Yemeni capital, Sana’a, and the governorates of Lahj, Taiz, Hodeidah, Saada and Hajjah. He had claimed in a post that the attacks left dozens of civilians dead and injured.The Houthi-affiliated Saba News Agency (Sana’a branch) has now reported, citing sources, that attacks on buses and trucks in Wadi Maabaq in Lahj Governorate left 25 people dead or missing and six injured. The Houthis have also reported fresh strikes on Sana’a and Hodeidah today, while claiming to have shot down a Saudi military reconnaissance aircraft.On the other hand, the Saudi-led military coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone launched towards the southern region. Saudi Civil Defence also issued multiple alerts last night for Jazan, Najran, Al Sulayyil and Abha.On the Iran front, Iranian state media reported yesterday that three oil tankers had exploded after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.On Monday, the US Treasury Department sanctioned more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies and key personnel in an effort to disrupt Iran’s global shadow banking networks. Moreover, the Department’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) identified approximately 14.7 billion dollars in financial activity between January 2025 and August 2026 that was potentially linked to Iranian shadow banking.As part of their compliance requirements, US financial institutions report suspicious activity to FinCEN, making the information available to law enforcement and national security agencies.

. On the first day of the 43rd Indian Oil Servo Surjit Hockey Tournament in Jalandhar yesterday, the Pool A match between former champions Indian Oil Mumbai and BSF Jalandhar ended in a 1- 1 draw.Bharat Petroleum registered a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Punjab National Bank (PNB), Delhi, in a Pool-B league match.In Pool-D, the Indian Air Force team delivered an impressive performance, securing victory over Punjab & Sind Bank, Delhi, 2-1.

. Major Asian stock market indices edged lower today. Taiwan’s Taiex shed over 6.2 per cent, South Korea’s Kospi slumped 5.2 per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell almost 5.1 per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times dipped nearly 2.1 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropped 1.9 per cent, and China’s Shanghai Composite dipped 1.2 per cent.On the economic front, Japan’s consumer price index (CPI) rose to 2.3 per cent year-on-year in October, up from 2.1 per cent in September. Consumer prices exceeded the Bank of Japan’s two per cent target for the second straight month. Meanwhile, the core CPI, which strips out prices of food, rose to 2.2 per cent last month on an annual basis, higher than 2.1 per cent in the previous month.In European markets, Germany’s DAX dipped 1.8 per cent, and London’s FTSE 100 dropped half a per cent, when reports last came in.

. Avishesh Jha won the first prize (Gold Award) at the inaugural edition of Prasar Bharati’s Script Pitching Lab, ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’, held at the Black Box, Kala Academy, Goa, as part of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026. Satyavyas secured the second position with the Silver Award, while Jitesh Thakur won the Bronze Award.The awards were presented by Prithul Kumar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting; Reena Sonowal, Director General, Doordarshan; and Dheeraj Singh, Managing Director, National Film Development Corporation (NFDC).The Gold Award carries a cash prize of ₹5 lakh, the Silver Award ₹3 lakh and the Bronze Award ₹2 lakh. Three Special Mention Awards, each carrying ₹50,000, were also presented.Prithul Kumar described the initiative as an important step towards engaging young creative talent and transforming public broadcasting through compelling storytelling. He emphasised that a strong script forms the foundation of successful filmmaking.Reena Sonowal highlighted the initiative’s role in nurturing emerging writers and connecting creative talent with the content production industry. She also appreciated the jury, organising team and media representatives for their contributions.The initiative received around 1,016 applications, from which 30 finalists were shortlisted to pitch their scripts before an eminent jury over three days. Through ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’, Prasar Bharati aims to promote original storytelling and bring diverse Indian stories to wider audiences.

. S&P Global has projected India to be one of the fastest-growing economies in the Asia-Pacific region in 2027. The agency expects India’s economy to grow by 7 per cent in both the current fiscal year and the next fiscal year, ending March 2028.In its Economic Outlook Asia-Pacific Q1 2027 report, the agency said India’s growth in the June and September quarters was driven by robust goods exports, government-led investment spending and strong household consumption, supported by buoyant credit growth.The global firm also highlighted India’s growing integration into global supply chains, noting that export performance had benefited from trade diversification and the country’s expanding role in global manufacturing. Electronics, engineering goods and chemicals were among the sectors that recorded particular strength.S&P Global projects inflation to average 5.3 per cent in the current fiscal year ending March 2027, with risks tilted to the upside. However, it expects inflation to ease to 4.7 per cent in the fiscal year ending March 2028.Against this backdrop, the agency expects the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to raise policy rates by a further 25 basis points in December. It also said the likelihood of another rate hike in early 2027 had increased.

. An earthquake measuring 5.6 on the local magnitude scale struck near Olangchung Gola in Nepal’s Taplejung district, close to the Nepal-Tibet border, at around 7:17 AM local time this morning.According to Nepal’s National Earthquake Monitoring and Research Centre, tremors were felt across neighbouring Sikkim, North Bengal and Bihar. In North Bengal, tremors were reported in Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Siliguri, Jalpaiguri and parts of North and South Dinajpur districts. Tremors were also felt in Bhutan and some areas of Bangladesh.The earthquake caused panic among residents in parts of North Bengal. However, no casualties have been reported.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today shared an article by Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Minister Jayant Chaudhary highlighting the country’s growing focus on skill development. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that in the article, Mr Chaudhary highlighted how initiatives like the upcoming World Skills Asia 2027 are preparing youth for emerging opportunities in the age of AI.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) yesterday proposed eliminating additional disclosure requirements for offshore funds, arguing that existing beneficial ownership disclosure norms already provide adequate transparency and oversight. The proposal marks a significant shift from regulations introduced in 2023, when the market regulator tightened scrutiny of offshore investment structures. Under the current framework, offshore funds considered to be at higher risk are required to make enhanced disclosures, including details of their ultimate beneficial owners.The regulator said the proposed changes are aimed at balancing regulatory oversight with ease of doing business while ensuring that capital markets remain attractive to foreign investors. The proposal has been put forward for public consultation, and feedback from market participants is expected before SEBI takes a final decision on amending the framework.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.
